title: Quarterly reservation runway & autoscale lab proposal
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: enterprise customers require predictable cost and latency for reserved GPU pools but also want burst capacity and lower unit costs. Current Dedicated offering exposes a hard trade-off between reservation runway (how long we prewarm) and cost efficiency. Goal: deliver a quarterly plan and runnable experiment slate (Autoscale Lab) that tests a small set of reservation strategies and guardrails to reduce cost per 100k tokens by >=10% while preserving latency SLOs for P95. The outcome will be a playbook (runbook + decision matrix) for production rollout and a prioritized set of console controls for customers (prewarm-window, hedge-reservoir-size, canary policies).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Experiment matrix defined with at least 4 strategies (predictive prewarm, reservoir hedging, burst-only pools, tiered fallthrough) and clear success metrics
A2: Runbook draft published in Confluence with operational steps for canaries and rollback
A3: Backend experiment infra tickets opened and scoped with ENG owners and estimates
A4: Telemetry dashboard (cost/unit, p50/p95 latency, queue length, GPU utilization) connected to experiment IDs
A5: Safety guardrails documented (max cost delta, probe rate limits, automatic fallback thresholds) and approved by SRE
A6: Stakeholder sign-off from Sales/Success on customer-facing phrasing for pilot enrollment
notes_and_updates: 2026-01-12: Kickoff with ENG, SRE, Solutions Eng. Agreed to limit initial lab to 3 accounts with representative workload profiles (chat, embeddings, reranking).
2026-01-20: Architecture spike complete. ENG noted need for a lightweight experiment flagging path and extra metrics for queue depth. Raised ENG-22111 for telemetry work.

2026-01-28: Trade-off discussion: predictive prewarm reduces cold-start P95 but increases steady-state cost. Decided to prioritize mixed reservoir + hedging strategy for first experiment because it gives best rollback path.

2026-02-04: Draft runbook v0.1 posted to Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DED/pages/AutoscaleLab-Runbook. Added steps for Canary window (1 hour, 10% traffic), rollback criteria, and incident playbook.
2026-02-10: Dependencies identified: ENG-47821 (autoscale-control-api), ENG-49200 (prefix-cache telemetry), PM-4219 (capacity-autoscaler-roadmap alignment). Added to dependencies list.
2026-02-15: SRE review feedback: require max 15% cost uplift threshold during canary and daily automated snapshotting of rollback metrics. Incorporated into runbook.
2026-02-22: Blocker: billing metric ingestion delay causes test cost estimates to be laggy by ~6 hours. Action: ENG to prioritize ingestion pipeline fix (ENG-50312).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: experiments increase unit cost temporarily and trigger customer alarms. Mitigation: limit canary exposure to 1 hour and 10% traffic; automated rollback on cost delta >15%
Risk: telemetry lag obscures leading indicators. Mitigation: prioritize ENG-50312 (billing ingestion) and add proxy metrics (queue length, GPU utilization) for near-real-time decisions
Risk: model variance causes noisy latency signals. Mitigation: use stable synthetic prompt set and per-model baselining before experiments
next_steps: 2) SRE: review and approve runbook fail-stop thresholds by 2026-02-25
3) PM: finalize pilot account list and invitation copy with Sales by 2026-02-29
4) Design/Console: prototype control toggles (prewarm window slider, reservoir size) and link to dashboard; mock due 2026-03-07
